blockingIssues.description: server/automation/shutdown.ts waits on automationMutex before calling server.close() / wss.close(), so the server can still accept fresh requests after SIGTERM/SIGINT while shutdown is blocked behind in-flight automation work.

server/automation/shutdown.ts exits with code 0 after Promise.allSettled(killPromises) without inspecting failed kill results or verifying that child PIDs are actually gone; on Windows killByPid/taskkill failures are swallowed.

server/shared/convexClient.ts treats every non-ConvexHttpError as retryable, so malformed 2xx JSON responses and other local exceptions can be retried even though the contract only allows network errors, HTTP 5xx, and 429.

Changing frontend/src/hooks/useAuthenticatedFetch.ts does not wire retry behavior into most authenticated API calls because the application still mostly calls apiFetch() directly via the module-level tokenGetter path.
frontend/src/hooks/useApiCall.ts is unused, so no UI actually renders loading/retrying state during retry backoff.
frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts disconnect() cancels a throwaway object instead of the live cancelled flag, so an in-flight async connect can still open a socket after an intentional disconnect.
frontend/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts cleanup closes sockets without clearing connected, so the hook can report connected === true after the socket is already gone.

python/core/errors/http_client.py does not synchronize OPEN → HALF_OPEN probe admission, so a shared ResilientHttpClient can admit multiple concurrent half-open probes instead of a single probe request.

python/core/shutdown.py rewrites the state file using placeholder set_state() values from entry points, which can overwrite richer in-session save_state() snapshots and lose current action/progress metadata.

Workflow and multi-account signal handling only call runner.stop() and do not directly register cleanup for active Playwright contexts, so browser contexts can remain open until long-running tasks unwind.

Two real Windows stop flows still use killByPid() -> taskkill /T /F (automation stop and manual profile stop), bypassing the new Python signal handlers and skipping graceful save_state()/cleanup entirely.
The reliability-verify transcript never proved the app loaded from the dev servers; it fell back to build success plus /api/health instead of validating the required app-load behavior.
Sentry validation stopped at grep-based init checks and did not prove frontend, server, and Python test events reached Sentry end-to-end.
